method_source: GraphRAG-style Local Evidence Aggregation: deterministic graph-window retrieval with the SA-MCGS local evidence schema, without relation-first memory, critical-pair revisiting, OC/core signals, or dynamic-core replacement.
deterministic_window_policy: one center node plus deterministic graph neighbors; fill by SCC order

conflicts.description: The acceleration of payment and loss of cure rights in 11.4.3 conflicts with the standard protections typically afforded during bankruptcy (13.2).
The negative covenant in 11.4.3 creates a high-stakes default trigger that is not clearly reconciled with the general liability limitations in 11.
Bidirectional reference suggests a circular dependency between expiration effects and royalty updates.
The restrictive covenant in 11.4.3 acts as a trigger for the material default and payment acceleration provisions in 13.2, creating a high-stakes dependency without a defined cure period.
Bidirectional dependency between price adjustments and purchase targets creates ambiguity regarding which clause takes precedence during contract year reconciliation.
The interaction between the strict default acceleration in 11.4.3 and the bankruptcy event in 13.2 creates a high-risk path with no apparent cure rights.
11.4.3 imposes strict liability and acceleration of payments for any upstream mismatch regarding asset liens/IP, which directly impacts the financial stability of the obligations in 2.2.
The Retooling and Development Costs clause (2.2) references cost details in 1.19, which contains a redaction/placeholder '[***]', rendering the cost provision underspecified.
Fundamental disagreement on termination mechanics: one clause provides a no-fee/cure-allowed path, while the other imposes fees and eliminates cure rights for the exact same path.
Potential overlap in expense categorization between 'other amounts' (1.115) and 'out-of-pocket costs' (1.19) due to vague definitions and redactions.
The pricing adjustment clause relies on a redacted/missing value [***] while being cyclically linked to the royalty update clause, preventing resolution of the financial terms.
Circular reference between expiration effects and payment obligations may lead to ambiguity regarding whether 'Development Purchases' are subject to settlement upon expiration.
The substantive restriction in 6.2 is linked to an empty clause 1.25, creating an unresolved reference that prevents full interpretation of the restriction.
The bidirectional references between purchase targets and out-of-pocket cost definitions create a circular dependency that lacks clear priority, potentially complicating financial audits.
The ownership clause (8.2) references the placeholder clause (1.25) which is currently undefined, creating a structural risk for contract interpretation.

The grant of rights in 9.2 is functionally constrained by the aggressive default and acceleration provisions in 11.4.3, creating a mismatch between the scope of the grant and the conditions for its termination.
